mechanism_claims.claim_text: rAtPDF2.3 directly blocks Kv1.2 and Kv1.6 potassium channels in Xenopus laevis oocytes; source text reports IC50 values of 1.3 ± 0.2 μM for Kv1.2 and 978 ± 113 nM for Kv1.6, with no activity on tested Nav channels at 5 μM and no effect on other tested Kv channels at 3 μM.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is potassium-channel block in the oocyte expression system; this is not promoted as the direct antifungal target in yeast.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: K33/G36 toxin-signature variants change Kv channel inhibitory potency: G36N increases potency, K33A reduces potency, and K33A/G36N has intermediate reported IC50 values against Kv1.2/Kv1.6.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: rAtPDF2.3 variants K33A, G36N, and K33A/G36N
mechanism_claims.limitations: Variant channel-blocking differences did not translate into significant antifungal potency differences against F. graminearum in the paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: S. cerevisiae potassium transport/homeostasis genes modulate tolerance to rAtPDF2.3; Table 2 hypersensitivity is interpreted as tolerance biology rather than proof that yeast potassium transporters are the direct antifungal target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: rAtPDF2.3 antifungal activity in S. cerevisiae
direct_assay_types: yeast knockout growth inhibition IC50 comparison
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper explicitly separates Kv-channel inhibition from antifungal potency; potassium homeostasis is retained as tolerance/context evidence only.
